Definition: delightful; hence, a delight, i.e. object of affection or desire
KeyPassages: Ezekiel 24:16; Ezekiel 24:21; Song of Solomon 5:16; Lamentations 1:10
BiblicalUsage: Machmad is the delight, the thing the eyes desire, and it is always the thing that can be taken away. Ezekiel 24:16 has God telling the prophet He will take away the desire of his eyes with a stroke, and Ezekiel 24:21 says He will profane the sanctuary, the desire of their eyes. Lamentations 1:10 says the adversary spread out his hand upon all her pleasant things, while Song of Solomon 5:16 turns the word toward the beloved, who is altogether lovely.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word warns me about what I call my delight: if it is a place or a person I hold tighter than God, it can be taken, and I will feel the loss. My position is that the only delight that cannot be taken is the one Song of Solomon 5:16 names, a beloved who is altogether lovely.
